subject: AI & Agents
title: GPT and the Age of Large Language Models
description: A fast breakdown of GPT and the Age of Large Language Models for builders.

hook.text: In 2020, OpenAI showed that scaling a language model to 175 billion parameters produces something eerie.

buildup.text: GPT-3 could write essays, code, poetry, and even legal briefs from a short prompt.

discovery.text: The recipe was simple: more data, more parameters, more compute. The results were not simple at all.

twist.text: Nobody fully understands why scaling works so well. Emergent abilities appear unpredictably.

climax.text: ChatGPT reached 100 million users in two months — the fastest-growing app in history.

punchline.text: Scale it up and surprising things happen.

quiz.question: What made GPT-3 surprising to researchers?
options: Scaling alone produced unexpected emergent abilities
It was the first neural network ever built
It could physically interact with the world

details.summary: GPT models, starting with GPT-1 in 2018, showed that scaling Transformers on massive text data produces increasingly capable language AI. GPT-3 and GPT-4 demonstrated emergent abilities that transformed the field.
details.whyItMatters: The GPT series proved that scale unlocks unexpected capabilities in language AI. This insight launched the modern LLM race and reshaped how billions of people interact with technology.
takeaways: GPT models scale Transformers on massive amounts of text data
Each generation showed surprising emergent capabilities
The GPT series launched the modern large language model era

faq.question: What is the progression from GPT-1 to GPT-4?
faq.answer: GPT-1 had 117 million parameters and showed basic language understanding. GPT-2 (1.5 billion) could generate coherent text. GPT-3 (175 billion) exhibited emergent abilities. GPT-4 added multimodal understanding.

faq.question: Why are GPT models called generative pre-trained transformers?
faq.answer: Generative because they produce text. Pre-trained because they learn from massive text data before any specific task training. Transformer because they use the Transformer architecture for processing text.
